prompt: For a reaction, ΔH = +40 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. At which temperature is the reaction spontaneous?

For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH⦵ = −92.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS⦵ = −199 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

**(a)** Explain the sign of ΔS⦵. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate ΔG⦵ at 298 K and comment on the spontaneity. **[2]**

**(c)** Calculate the temperature above which the reaction is no longer spontaneous. **[1]**

**(d)** Calculate the equilibrium constant at 298 K. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Four moles of gas become two, so the dispersal of matter decreases ✓

**(b)** $\Delta G = -92.2 - 298(-0.199) = -32.9\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ ✓; negative, so spontaneous at 298 K ✓

**(c)** $T = \tfrac{92.2}{0.199} = 463\ \text{K}$ ✓

**(d)** $\ln K = \tfrac{32\,900}{8.31\times298} = 13.3$ ✓; $K \approx 6\times10^5$ ✓
